views.name: superhero_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.full_name AS full_name,
  s.gender_id AS gender_id,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  s.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,

  s.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero s
views.description: One row per superhero with canonical identity and foreign-key ids for joins (clean projection of core superhero attributes).

views.name: superhero_with_colour_names
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  ce.colour AS eye_colour,
  ch.colour AS hair_colour,
  cs.colour AS skin_colour
FROM superhero AS s
LEFT JOIN colour AS ce ON s.eye_colour_id = ce.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS ch ON s.hair_colour_id = ch.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS cs ON s.skin_colour_id = cs.id
views.description: Denormalized hero-level view that attaches eye, hair, and skin colour names to each superhero row for easy textual filtering and presentation.

views.name: superhero_basic_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id,
  s.superhero_name,
  s.full_name,
  s.gender_id,
  g.gender AS gender,
  s.publisher_id,
  p.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  s.alignment_id,
  a.alignment AS alignment,
  s.race_id,
  r.race AS race,
  s.eye_colour_id,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  s.hair_colour_id,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,
  s.skin_colour_id,
  sc.colour AS skin_colour,
  s.height_cm,
  s.weight_kg
FROM superhero_core s
LEFT JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN colour ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
views.description: One row per superhero with primary identifying and demographic columns joined to their referenced lookup labels (gender, publisher, alignment, race, eye/hair/skin colours). Useful as a denormalized superhero master for filtering, display, and further aggregation.

views.name: hero_attribute_values
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.id AS hero_id,
  h.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  h.full_name AS full_name,
  a.id AS attribute_id,
  a.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value AS attribute_value
FROM superhero AS h
JOIN hero_attribute AS ha
  ON h.id = ha.hero_id
JOIN attribute AS a
  ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
views.description: Denormalized row-level relation of each hero's attribute values, joining hero, attribute, and hero_attribute so each row is a single attribute measurement for a single superhero.

  id AS superhero_id,
  height_cm,
  weight_kg
FROM
  superhero_core

views.name: superhero_with_attributes_and_powers_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.weight_kg AS weight_kg,
  s.height_cm AS height_cm,
  COALESCE(p.num_powers, 0) AS num_powers,
  COALESCE(a.num_attributes, 0) AS num_attributes
FROM superhero s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT hero_id, COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) AS num_powers
  FROM hero_power
  GROUP BY hero_id
) p ON s.id = p.hero_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT hero_id, COUNT(DISTINCT attribute_id) AS num_attributes
  FROM hero_attribute
  GROUP BY hero_id
) a ON s.id = a.hero_id
views.description: Per-superhero aggregated measures: counts of linked powers and attributes plus raw measures. Useful for questions that rank or filter heroes by capability breadth while preserving one row per hero.

views.name: superhero_colour_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS id,
  s.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  s.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  s.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  s.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  CASE
    WHEN s.eye_colour_id IS NOT NULL
     AND s.hair_colour_id IS NOT NULL
     AND s.skin_colour_id IS NOT NULL
     AND s.eye_colour_id = s.hair_colour_id
     AND s.eye_colour_id = s.skin_colour_id
    THEN 1
    WHEN s.eye_colour_id IS NULL
     OR s.hair_colour_id IS NULL
     OR s.skin_colour_id IS NULL
    THEN 0
    WHEN s.eye_colour_id = s.hair_colour_id
     AND s.eye_colour_id = s.skin_colour_id
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS all_colours_equal
FROM superhero s
views.description: Cohort of superheroes annotated with whether all three colour FK columns are equal. One row per superhero. Useful for queries that look for matching or differing eye/hair/skin colours.
